pageCache.pageTitle: Blandford St Mary Church of England Primary School - Home
pageCache.text:
Love, Hope, Perseverance, Respect, Responsibility
Blandford St Mary
Welcome to Blandford St Mary Church of England Primary School. I feel immensely proud to be the Headteacher of this wonderful one-form entry school where children truly are at the heart of everything we do.
We offer excellent standards of care, guidance and support and a high-quality learning environment to support all learners equally. The school upholds an ethos of high expectations which provides children with challenging opportunities where children acquire skills, knowledge and confidence that can be applied to all future learning experiences. These opportunities encourage respect, self-belief, excellence and enjoyment and prepare our pupils for the next stage of their education.
Useful Links
Latest News
Follow Us
From their very first day of school...to their final day of Year 6. Look how much they've grown. From little faces filled with wonder to the incredible children they are today, it has been a privilege to watch them learn, grow, laugh and make memories along the way. Now, they're ready for their next adventure... We are so incredibly proud of you all Year 6. Go out into the world, be brave, be kind, seize new opportunities and challenges and make it a better place.
What a successful and fun-filled two days of Forest School. Our children enjoyed a wonderful range of hands-on activities: woodwork, cooking, natural art, bug stations, seed planting and clay mindfulness. Two days filled with creativity, curiosity, learning and plenty of outdoor fun. A huge thank you to our wonderful Miss Maese for planning, organising and resourcing such a fun-filled experience for all our children. Also our parent volunteers, who were absolutely brilliant. Such a memorable time for all. #education #outdooreducation #forestschool #happychildren #creativity
Sun, sea, smiles and so many happy memories! Our annual whole-school beach trip was a fantastic day filled with fun and laughter. We enjoyed paddling and splashing in the sea, digging holes in the sand, building amazing sandcastles and sharing lunch together under the gazebos. We finished the day with well-deserved ice creams and ice lollies! A wonderful day of friendship, teamwork and making memories together. #beachday #schooltrip #makingmemories #fun #happychildren
Healthy Lunch Challenge! In Design & Technology, Year 3 explored what makes a healthy lunch by using the Eatwell Plate as their guide. They analysed different lunch ideas, planned balanced meals, prepared a variety of foods, then tasted and evaluated each one. A fun way to build cooking skills, make healthy choices and learn through practical experience! #education #year3 #dt #healthychoices #foodpreparation
In DT, our Year 1 children learned all about preparing food safely. They practised good hygiene, carefully prepared their own healthy salads and then enjoyed eating them together outside in the sunshine. A hands-on lesson full of learning, teamwork and healthy choices! #designtechnology #Year1 #healthyeating #foodpreparation #primaryschool
**Read to the Beat this Summer!** This summer, we're encouraging all our pupils to take part in the **Summer Reading Challenge 2026** at our local library! Reading over the six-week holidays helps children: Keep their reading skills sharp Grow their imagination and creativity Build confidence and vocabulary Discover exciting new stories and characters Just a few minutes of reading each day can make a big difference and help children return to school ready to learn. Visit our local library, sign up for the **Read to the Beat** Summer Reading Challenge and enjoy a summer full of books, music and fun! Happy reading! #summerreading #schoolcommunity #library #youngreaders #primaryschool
What a fantastic afternoon for our KS2 girls! A huge thank you to Steph and Tom from AFC Bournemouth Community Sports Trust for visiting our school and delivering free football coaching sessions for our Year 4, 5 and 6 girls. The girls had an amazing time taking part in the different games, developing new skills and learning from their expert advice. Their enthusiasm, teamwork and smiles said it all! Thank you for inspiring the next generation of footballers- we can't wait to welcome you back! #football #girlsfootball #primaryschool #afcbournemouth #communitysport
Last week, we had the pleasure of hosting a Thank You Tea to celebrate our amazing school volunteers. Your dedication, kindness and commitment make our school a better place every single day. Whether you give your time in the classroom, on trips, at events, or behind the scenes, your support makes a real difference. We are so grateful for everything you do. Thank you for being such an important part of our school community- we appreciate you all! #thankyou #primaryschool #community #volunteer #dedication
We're still not over our incredible Year 6 production of Matilda Jr! The wonderful @bellawest_photography has just released these amazing photographs and we think you'll agree- they've captured every magical moment! We were so lucky to have had such a talented professional photographer preserve these memories. We were also delighted to welcome our Academy CEO, Mr Lacey, to watch our performance. We hope he enjoyed it as much as the children did. We're so incredibly proud of our Year 6 stars #matilda #year6 #schoolproduction #makingmemories #happychildren
WHAT A SHOW! Our Year 6 production of Matilda Jr at Clayesmore Theatre was an unforgettable experience from start to finish. We felt incredibly lucky to have performed in such a wonderful venue and are so grateful to Clayesmore School for allowing us to use their theatre free of charge. Over the past six weeks, the children have worked tirelessly, learning lines, songs and choreography both at school and at home- and it truly paid off. Their confidence, talent and teamwork shone on stage, leaving us all amazed and incredibly proud. Miss West and I couldn't be any prouder of each and every single one of them. Bravo Year 6, you were absolutely phenomenal. A huge thank you to our talented photographer for capturing these beautiful pictures Bella West These wonderful photos will help us treasure this special performance for years to come. #schoolproduction #matilda #performing #theatre #liveshow
During Sports Week, our wonderful School Council organised a sponsored marathon, with children taking part in class sessions. Thanks to the incredible generosity of our parents and carers, we raised an amazing amount of money! This fantastic achievement means we can install a large slide on the hill in our school field for everyone to enjoy. A huge thank you to everyone who supported this fundraiser- your kindness and generosity will make a lasting difference to our children. #primaryschool #sportsweek #schoolcouncil #fundraising #thankyou
Our Reception Class had some very special visitors- adorable baby rabbits! A huge thank you to Cara Roff for bringing them to school and giving the children a memorable experience. The children loved meeting, observing and gently handling the rabbits, showing kindness and curiosity. Experiences like these bring learning to life, helping children develop their understanding of the natural world. #reception #earlyyears #rabbits #handsonlearning
Friday marked the end of our fantastic Sports Week with an amazing Sports Day! What a brilliant day it was, with a wonderful atmosphere from start to finish. The children enjoyed a carousel of activities before taking part in some exciting races, ensuring everyone had the opportunity to be involved and have fun. At lunchtime, we came together for a whole school picnic with parents and carers, making it a truly special occasion for our school community. Well done to all the children~ we are so proud of you all. A HUGE thank you to Miss West for organising such a successful Sports Week. Your hard work and dedication ensured the week was inclusive, engaging and most of all FUN for every child. #sportsweek #sportsday #inclusion #everychildmatters #fun
Thursday of Sports Week saw an exciting Boogie Bounce Session! I'm sure you've heard about this at home already! (Even I snuck on to have ago!) This had to be a highlight, the children absolutely loved taking part and had so much fun bouncing, moving and burning off energy. Our incredible instructor was enthusiastic and energetic, making the sessions great fun for all. A huge thank you to our Friends of School for subsiding this fantastic activity and helping us create such a memorable experience for our children. #primaryschool #boogiebounce #trampoline #funtimes #happychildren
Sports Week- Wednesday edition! It was all about fast serves, quick reflexes and team spirit as children took on tennis and dodgeball. From powerful shots to epic dodges, the energy was incredible. A huge thank you to the tennis coach, from Blandford Tennis Club, who gave his whole day free of charge. #sportsweek #primaryschool #tennis #dodgeball #thankyou

pageCache.text:
Sport Premium
Impact and Sustainability
The Sport Premium funding has had a significant influence on our whole school development. We have taken huge steps forward in promoting education, school sport and active lifestyles through this funding. A key factor in our planning of the sport premium budget has been ‘variety’, where we believe that all pupils should be provided with a varied, active and engaging curriculum in Sport. For example pupils now have opportunities in: orienteering, golf, sailing, wind-surfing, paddle boarding.
Staff training has identified areas for development and provided opportunities for staff to expand their knowledge in order to offer high quality PE lessons. Teaching Assistants have had bespoke CPD in Invasion Games and Striking and Fielding Games. All staff had CPD in Invasion Games and Gymnastics.
We have adapted from a mainly single sports provider to gain a range of opportunities for both children and staff. We have been ever present at all of the local sporting events which we are invited to. Our development of intra-school provision has influenced our playtimes. Over the past 12 months we have had no significant behaviour issues. Children look forward to their sessions on the Astro, Basketball zone or Fitness Centre.
Sports Funding
All primary schools in England receive a grant from the Department for Education. All schools in receipt of the grant are obliged to publish on their websites details of how they spend their PE and sport grant. This must include details about the impact this funding has on pupils’ PE and sport participation and attainment.
Further information is available by clicking in the links below.

Starting Reception
Starting Reception is an exciting milestone for both children and families. To help make this transition as smooth and positive as possible, we have gathered together a range of useful information and resources to support you and your child as they prepare to begin school life at Blandford St Mary Primary School.
We recommend exploring the Starting Reception – Early Years Toolkit, which offers a range of helpful activities, videos and guidance for families with children starting Reception.
You are warmly invited to book a tour. This will be an informal and welcoming opportunity for families to see our school in action, with a member of the leadership team available to guide you around the school and answer any questions you may have

pageCache.text:
Christian Distinctiveness
Collective Worship
Collective Worship at our school is highly valued, with time set apart each day for the whole school community to gather together in a time of reflection, to have the opportunity to engage with their own spirituality, to learn about the Biblical teachings and further explore our school's vision and values. During these special times, the school is still, quiet and respectful. For an overview of our collective worships please refer to the files at the bottom of this page.
All worship begins with the lighting of our three candles and saying our welcoming words.
Harvest
This year, we have once again held a whole school harvest service to celebrate God's goodness in creation. During our harvest service, we thanked God for providing us with the resources to grow such a wide variety of delicious foods in our world. We also took the opportunity to thank the people who grow and harvest our foods - mums and dads in their allotments and the farmers in their fields.
Our school community collected food items to donate to the Blandford Foodbank. As you can see from the picture below, our families, once again, have been extremely generous in their donations to help others. Thank you.
Christingle
In our Christingle Service we heard that Jesus said, Christians are ‘the light of the world’ (Matthew 5.14-16) and that they should love the world like God does.
Christians are called to be a shining light for those people who are in dark places and Christians are called to love everyone, particularly if they are having a bad time.
No matter what we believe, we can all be shining lights and show love to those who are in need of it.
Spirituality at Blandford St Mary
At Blandford St Mary CE Primary School, we believe that spiritual development is a fundamental aspect of children's personal growth and well-being. It is not limited to any faith or religious belief, but is something that can be experienced through learning, play, and everyday life.
Spirituality is not something we can see — it is something we feel inside. It shapes how we understand ourselves, how we relate to others, how we experience the world, and how we explore the mystery and wonder of life.
We aim for all children to develop holistically so that they become happy, fulfilled, spiritually aware, and socially and emotionally engaged.
For further detail, please refer to our Spirituality Definition and our Spirituality Policy at the bottom of this section.

Governance
DSAT TRUST BOARD
We are members of the Diocese of Salisbury Academy Trust and the governance of the Trust belongs to the main DSAT Board. Below is our Scheme of Delegation. This also includes our Constitution and Terms of Reference. Paper copies can be obtained through the school office or by using the contact us option on this website. You can also find details of the Trust Board and details of our Trust Governance by clicking here.
Welcome to our Academy Standards and Ethos Committee (ASEC)
The ASEC works alongside the Headteacher and senior leadership team to set the strategic direction of the school and monitors the impact of the school improvement plan in a variety of ways. ASEC members volunteer their time and are a key part of the school's leadership team.
The Academy Standards and Ethos Committee are bound by a Scheme of Delegation, Constitution and Terms of Reference. These documents provide the set of rules by which the local Governors abide in supporting DSAT to take responsibility for the School and a copy of this document is attached here.
If you would like to contact the Chair of the Academy Standards and Ethos Committee or its Clerk, please email Clerk@blandfordstmary.dsat.org.uk or call into the school office and leave a request.
Paper copies of ASEC meetings can be obtained through the school office or by using the ‘contact us’ option on this website. You can also find details of the Trust Board and details of our Trust Governance by clicking the link:Diocese of Salisbury Academy Trust - Governance

SEND
Special Educational Needs and Disability
At Blandford St Mary Primary School we use the definition for SEN and for disability from the SEND Code of Practice (2014) and the Equality Act (2010).
“A child or young person has special educational needs if he or she has a learning difficulty or disability which calls for special educational provision to be made for him or her. A learning difficulty or disability is a significantly greater difficulty in learning than the majority of others of the same age. Special educational provision means educational or training provision that is additional to, or different from, which is made generally for others of the same age in a mainstream setting in England.”
Disability
“Many children and young people who have SEN may have a disability under the Equality Act 2010 -that is ‘A physical or mental impairment which has a long-term and substantial adverse effect on their ability to carry out normal day-to-day activities.”
Mrs Katie Drake is the SENDCo at Blandford St Mary.
Contact- sen@blandfordstmary.dsat.org.uk
The designated governor for SEND is Mrs Sarah Granados.

Curriculum
At Blandford St Mary Primary School, we provide a broad, balanced and ambitious curriculum that builds carefully on the knowledge, understanding and skills of all children, regardless of their starting points. Our curriculum meets the statutory requirements of the Early Years Foundation Stage Framework and the Primary National Curriculum (2014), while also offering rich experiences and opportunities that respond to the learning and developmental needs of our pupils.
As a school community, our curriculum is driven by our core values of Aspiration, Communication and Curiosity. These principles underpin our curriculum intent and guide our approach to teaching and learning, encouraging children to aim high, express themselves confidently and develop a lifelong love of learning. At Blandford St Mary Primary School, we are committed to supporting the development of the whole child, ensuring that academic achievement sits alongside personal growth, wellbeing and character development.

pageCache.text:
SIAMS
The Statutory Inspection of Anglican and Methodist Schools (SIAMS) is the Church of England and Methodist Church’s outworking of the requirements of section 48 of the Education Act 2005. It is a key element of the life of all Church of England and Methodist schools in England.
Approximately every five years, schools are subject to an inspection which explores the question, “How effective is the school’s distinctive Christian vision, established and promoted by leadership at all levels, in enabling pupils and adults to flourish?” This overarching inspection question is examined through seven strands: 1. Vision and Leadership 2. Wisdom, Knowledge, and Skills 3. Character Development: Hope, Aspiration, and Courageous Advocacy 4. Community and Living Well Together 5. Dignity and Respect 6. Impact of Collective Worship 7. Effectiveness of Religious Education.
